title: Put on love (Colossians 3:12–17)
hook: clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, patience
tomorrow: what does faith look like in a pair of old work gloves?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a riddle solved: dead as a done deal, and the attention set on things above, then carried into the kitchen. Yesterday's line: things above.

Some mornings people dress for who they're trying to be: the interview shirt, the running shoes not yet worn. Is that fake, or a start? Is a kind word you don't feel yet a lie, or a first step? Christians argue about that very question with today's verses. Paul has just told the Colossians to take off anger and lying like old clothes. Now he opens the wardrobe: "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering."
screen: `DRESSED FOR WHO YOU'RE TRYING TO BE.` → `FAKE, OR A START?` → `PUT ON THEREFORE.`

segments.voice: Bowels of mercies is the old way of saying compassion felt in the gut. Then the hardest piece: "Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye." And the top layer: "And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness." Charity here is love, the bond that holds the outfit together. So can love be put on before it's felt? Two views, both inside the faith. The first says yes. In this passage love is something done: forbear, forgive. Put the clothes on, and over time they shape the one wearing them. Wait for the feeling, and you may wait forever. The second says slow down and look at the order. Holy and beloved comes before a single garment. The clothes come after being loved, not in place of it. Skip that, and love can turn into a performance, a smile over a grudge. Both are reading the same verse. And both keep this: love goes on last, over everything, and nobody wears these clothes alone in a room. Then the scene widens: the peace of God ruling in the heart, and a church "teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs." Love, it turns out, also gets sung.
screen: `BOWELS OF MERCIES: COMPASSION.` · `ABOVE ALL, CHARITY: THE BOND.` · `VIEW ONE: PUT IT ON, IT SHAPES YOU.` · `VIEW TWO: BELOVED FIRST, THEN CLOTHES.` · then, large: `ABOVE ALL, LOVE.`

segments.voice: Touch the things you're wearing one at a time, slowly: a sleeve, a collar, a shoe. With each one, name a word from Paul's list, kindness, meekness, patience, and with the last one, love. Go slowly enough that each word gets a breath of its own, and if someone who'll test your patience today comes to mind, let the last layer go on over them too.
Put on love. The last layer in Colossians three: love over compassion, kindness and patience, the bond that holds them together.
The line to keep: above all, love, put on by people already called beloved. Rest well.

howItsDone: Colossians 3:12–17 is a reading some couples choose for their weddings, and some Christians use the list of virtues as a short morning check.

pairs: love, the bond of the rest

myth: Paul lists love as one virtue among many, in no special place
"above all these things put on charity": love goes on last, over everything.
'charity' in this verse means giving money
here charity is love, the bond that holds the other virtues together.
"if any man have a quarrel against any": he plans for it, and asks for forgiving.

fork.setup: you think love can be put on before it's felt. your friend says that's just a costume. what's the strongest version of her view, from the verse?
options: the clothes come after 'holy and beloved'; skip that, and love can become a performance.
Paul never mentions feelings at all, so love is only about how things look.
Paul says to wait until the anger is gone before trying to be kind.
fork.reveal: her best case is in the order of the verse: beloved first, then the garments. yours is in the verbs: forbear, forgive, put on. both are reading the same lines.

original.note: Greek: bond, something that binds together, in Colossians 3:14.

trapdoor: what you thought: put on love means pretending to feel loving.
what it means: love is the last garment, over compassion, kindness and patience, worn around other people by those already called beloved.
what a scholar hears: charity is called the bond of perfectness, what ties the other virtues together; and readers still weigh whether the feeling or the doing comes first.
guess: love worn over every other virtue, holding them together
a warm feeling that arrives on its own, or not at all
a polite smile worn so nobody sees you're upset
recall: aim the attention on things above

chat.says: pop and dad fought over pop's recliner. dad says be extra sweet to pop. i'm not feeling it. fake?
options: Not if it starts from being loved. Beloved first, then put on love. Doing it can be a start.
Yes, it's fake. Paul says show love only once the warm feeling is already there.
Act sweet and keep the grudge inside. Paul only cares about how it looks outside.
chat.meaning: The clothes come after 'holy and beloved,' and love goes on over everything. Christians differ on feeling or doing first; neither means a smile over a grudge.

bowels of mercies.meaning: old English for compassion felt deep inside

longsuffering.meaning: patience that lasts a long time
